text: 最好别在小姐姐面前提尊严。
en: Best not to bring up dignity in front of a young lady.

text: 小姐姐的禁止事项能写一行半，长得丑的亲个嘴都不准。
en: A young lady's list of forbidden things could fill a line and a half — an ugly bloke isn't even allowed a kiss.

text: 打工人敢不敢把禁加班、禁扣工资、禁辱骂、禁半路加活、先给钱再干写在简历上？
en: Would wage workers dare put 'no forced overtime, no wage deductions, no abuse, no mid-job extra tasks, pay up front before work' on their CV?

text: 卖淫合法化降低不了强奸率。
en: Legalising prostitution won't lower the rape rate.

text: 因为强奸犯不是因为没钱没妓女才去强奸，而是因为他自己本人变态。
en: Because rapists don't rape for lack of money or prostitutes, but because they themselves are perverts.

text: 大同案变相的提供了一个执法层面的漏洞，使原本明朗的钱色交易判定方式，变得不再清晰。
en: The Datong case has, in effect, opened up a loophole at the law-enforcement level, muddying what was once a clear way of identifying sex-for-money transactions.

text: 就不知道这个漏洞什么时候补上了，那就是：借着订婚礼金的名义，支付嫖资。
en: One simply doesn't know when this loophole will be closed: namely, paying for prostitution under the pretext of engagement gift money.

text: 因为大同案证明了一点：1、订婚不具备任何法律意义；2、不能代表女性的性同意，但如果女性同意也不冲突；3、可以证明男性有结婚意愿。
en: Because the Datong case proved a few points: 1. engagement carries no legal significance; 2. it cannot stand for a woman's sexual consent, though if the woman agrees it is not contradictory; 3. it can prove the man's intention to marry.

text: 不知道各位最近是否在外网上经常看到国内一些咯咯哒，全国飞做业务的帖子或者记录视频，http://X.com上一搜一大把。
en: I wonder if you've lately been seeing, on the foreign internet, posts or recorded videos from certain 'cluck-clucks' within the country who fly all over to do business — search http://X.com and you'll find piles of them.

text: 操作方式大致为：第一步、借着相亲的名号约客人；第二步、咯咯哒去男方所在地见面；第三步、男方给钱，名义是订婚礼金；第四步、开始工作；第五步、完事后一拍两散，男方表示礼金不用退了，咯咯哒表示相亲失败好聚好散，下次有缘再见。
en: The modus operandi is roughly this: step one, arrange to meet clients under the banner of matchmaking; step two, the cluck-cluck travels to the man's city to meet him; step three, the man hands over money, nominally as engagement gift money; step four, the work begins; step five, once done they go their separate ways — the man says the gift money needn't be returned, the cluck-cluck says the matchmaking failed, they part on amicable terms, and hope to meet again if fate allows.

text: 整个过程，帽子叔叔很难抓尾巴，
en: Throughout the whole process, the police find it very hard to catch them out,

text: 质问她为啥不停找男人，她说在相亲；
en: Question her on why she keeps chasing men, and she says she's matchmaking;

text: 问她为啥不结婚但是钱不退，她说订婚又不代表同意，并且男方愿意；
en: Ask her why she won't marry yet won't return the money, and she says engagement doesn't mean consent, and the man is willing;

text: 问她为啥一相亲就钻宾馆，她说自己有性自由欲望大，找对象需要试床；
en: Ask her why she heads straight to a hotel the moment she matchmakes, and she says she's freely sexual with a strong libido, and needs to test the bed when seeking a partner;

text: 问她为啥介绍别的女的卖，她说自己相亲同时也给姐妹介绍对象，然后别的咯咯哒也是同样的操作。
en: Ask her why she pimps out other women, and she says that while she matchmakes she also finds partners for her sisters, and that other cluck-clucks operate the same way.

text: 这个漏洞在于：男方以订婚的名义给钱，女方再拒绝继续结婚，然后男方放弃给的钱，这就完成了一次转移支付，并且名义上是找不到漏洞的。
en: This loophole works as follows: the man pays under the pretext of engagement, the woman then refuses to proceed with the marriage, and the man gives up the money paid — thereby completing a transfer of funds, and on paper no loophole can be found.

text: 别问我为啥知道的，那些帖子里直接把聊天记录都亮出来了，玩的就是一个有恃无恐......
en: Don't ask me how I know — those posts lay the chat logs right out in the open; what they're playing at is sheer, unashamed brazenness...

text: PS：很多人貌似还不理解其中的问题，扯什么自由裁量权，执法层面所谓自由裁量权的前提，是有违法行为的事实或者证据，哪怕是非常微小的证据。
en: PS: many people still seem not to grasp the problem, going on about discretionary power. Yet the premise of so-called discretion at the enforcement level is the existence of facts or evidence of an unlawful act — however trivial the evidence.

text: 但是上述这种模式下，所有行为都是光明正大来的，甚至于开房都是去正规酒店实名制开房，聊天记录里谈的就是相亲介绍的事情。
en: But under the model described above, every act is done in broad daylight; even booking rooms is done at proper hotels under real-name registration, and the chat logs are all about matchmaking introductions.

text: 除非当面商谈的过程有录音，否则根本没证据。
en: Unless the face-to-face negotiation was recorded, there is simply no evidence.

text: 除了那种一天“相亲”好几个，每次都“试床”且连续大半年的（估计是欠债太狠），可能涉及聚众YL，不然怎么抓？
en: Save for those who 'matchmake' several times a day, 'test the bed' each time, and keep it up for over half a year (presumably up to their eyes in debt) — which might involve group YL — how else would you catch them?

text: 当然，不是所有都是那种可以全国飞到处“相亲”的，几百块站街的那种也并未消失。
en: Of course, not all are the sort who can fly across the country to 'matchmake' wherever they go; the street-walking kind going for a few hundred yuan hasn't vanished either.

text: 但未来女性的化债需求只会越来越多，必然会在法律的灰色地带找出路。
en: But women's future need to clear debt will only grow, and they will inevitably seek a way out in the grey areas of the law.

text: （叠个甲，卖钩子化债的男的也是有的，尤其是某些城市还不少，但还是远少于女的，毕竟男的卖钩子的基本要求可不低）
en: (A pre-emptive caveat: there are also men who clear debt by selling themselves, and in certain cities quite a few of them, but still far fewer than women — after all, the basic bar for a man selling himself is hardly low.)

text: 国内目前由于生育率的压力，不可能打击婚介行业；国家也不可能回到当年组织分配婚姻的时代，那么这个灰色地带就不可能消失。
en: At present, given the pressure of the birth rate, the state cannot crack down on the matchmaking industry; nor can it return to the era of state-arranged marriages, so this grey area cannot disappear.

text: 在包养和彩礼面前很难说卖淫和这俩有多大区别再加上一个代孕
en: Against mistressing and bride price, it's hard to say prostitution differs all that much from those two — and then there's surrogacy on top.

text: 很多支持合法的人，要的不是合法，而是制度的逻辑自洽，基于几个最根本的诉求和目标，保证各个部分法律解释的连贯性和一致性。
en: Many who support legalisation don't actually want legalisation, but rather logical self-consistency in the system — grounded in a few fundamental demands and goals, ensuring coherence and consistency across all parts of legal interpretation.

text: 本质不是支持卖淫，而是反对双标。
en: The essence isn't supporting prostitution, but opposing double standards.

text: 恩格斯在《私有制、家庭、国家的起源》里说： 婚姻和卖淫的区别不过是批发和零售。
en: Engels, in The Origin of the Family, Private Property and the State, said: the difference between marriage and prostitution is merely wholesale versus retail.

text: 夫妻双方都是在卖淫，而以妻子为常见。
en: Both husband and wife are prostituting themselves, with the wife being the more common case.

text: 只有双方之间不存在经济关系了，才是真正的婚姻。
en: Only when there is no economic relationship between the two parties is it a true marriage.

text: 如果把（1）包养（2）以谈恋爱、婚姻名义单方面收彩礼、索取礼物、索取房产份额，而不给予同等经济价值回馈的行为统一按照卖淫处置，相信大家都支持卖淫违法。
en: If (1) being kept, and (2) unilaterally taking bride price, gifts, and property shares under the guise of romance or marriage, without giving back equal economic value, were all uniformly treated as prostitution, I believe everyone would support making prostitution unlawful.

text: 同理，禁止代孕也是双标的一部分。
en: Likewise, the ban on surrogacy is also part of the double standard.

text: 你先回答我这个问题:女性的身体到底是不是女性自由支配的？
en: First answer me this: does a woman's body ultimately belong to her own free disposal?

text: 就是说，有没有一种可能，确实有爱慕虚荣又懒得通过劳动赚钱的女性？
en: That is to say, is it not possible that there genuinely are vain women who can't be bothered to earn through labour?

text: 有没有一种可能确实有自愿卖身的女性？
en: Is it not possible that there genuinely are women who sell themselves of their own free will?

text: 没人逼她强迫她，她纯粹出于内驱力而从事这项服务。
en: No one forces or coerces her; she engages in this service purely out of her own internal drive.

text: 女性有想不给谁睡就不给谁睡的权利，也有想跟谁睡就跟谁睡的权利，怎么在这个基础上加上钱就违法了？
en: A woman has the right to refuse sleep with whomever she pleases, and the right to sleep with whomever she pleases — so how does adding money on top of that become unlawful?

text: 包养不违法；约炮不违法；谈恋爱时转账加睡觉，也不违法；结婚时给彩礼加睡觉，还不违法；怎么卖淫就违法？
en: Being kept isn't unlawful; casual hook-ups aren't unlawful; transferring money and sleeping together while dating isn't unlawful; giving bride price and sleeping together in marriage still isn't unlawful — so how is prostitution unlawful?

text: 说明一下:我的疑问只是针对法律。
en: To be clear: my doubts are directed at the law alone.

text: 我不支持任何人去卖淫及嫖娼
en: I do not support anyone going into prostitution or patronising prostitutes.

text: 卖淫和合法了强奸犯会变少，怎么不说没有法律就没有犯罪呢
en: If legalising prostitution means fewer rapists, why not say there'd be no crime without laws?

text: 你没法反驳
en: You can't refute it.

text: 因为真正推动这个的，是女人。
en: Because the ones truly pushing this are women.

text: 也就是大家通常所谓的“潜在受害者”。
en: That is, the so-called 'potential victims' everyone talks about.

text: 当“受害者”哭着喊着说禁令是“压迫”的时候
en: When the 'victim' weeps and wails that the ban is 'oppression',

text: 你还能说什么呢？
en: what more can you say?

text: 卖淫的非法化运动和合法化运动一样
en: The movement to criminalise prostitution, like the movement to legalise it,

text: 都是以“女性主义”为主轴，随着她们的诉求变化而改变的，和男人的需求无关
en: is centred on 'feminism', shifting with their demands, and has nothing to do with men's needs.

text: 阶段一：卖淫是男权产物，必须取缔（女权1.0）我国在这个时代
en: Stage one: prostitution is a product of patriarchy and must be abolished (feminism 1.0) — our country is in this era.

text: 早期的西方女权，和中国女权一样，出于“女权=反对男人”的初级阶段，她们认为妓女的存在就是让男人爽到了，所以必须取缔，于是各国出台法律，关停妓院，禁止卖淫嫖娼
en: Early Western feminism, like Chinese feminism, sat at the primitive stage of 'feminism = opposing men'; they held that the existence of prostitutes merely gratified men, so it had to be abolished. Countries thus enacted laws, shut down brothels, and banned prostitution and patronising prostitutes.

text: 阶段二：卖，是女性自由，买，是男性压迫（女权2.0）西方国家主要在这个时代
en: Stage two: selling is women's freedom, buying is male oppression (feminism 2.0) — Western countries are mainly in this era.

text: 还是那句话“女人的身体女人做主”“女性不被定义”“女性拒绝标签”，在女权运动的进化助推下，卖淫不再是“女性道德低下的表现”，（说起来也没错，传统道德观确实是男权时代建立的，对于女性的性权益是有严格的规训的，妓女就是这么被定位为不道德的存在的。
en: As the saying goes, 'a woman's body is hers to command', 'women are not to be defined', 'women reject labels'. Bolstered by the evolution of the feminist movement, prostitution is no longer 'a sign of women's moral degeneracy' (and to be fair, traditional morality was indeed built in the patriarchal age, imposing strict discipline on women's sexual rights, which is precisely how prostitutes came to be labelled immoral.

text: 实际上延伸一下来看，所有的“不道德”都是如此）
en: Taken a step further, all 'immorality' is like this.)

text: 因此各国政府解禁了卖淫，但是男性整不出这些花活，所以嫖依旧还是违法的
en: Thus governments around the world decriminalised prostitution, but men couldn't pull off such tricks, so buying remains unlawful.

text: 是的，如今欧美很多国家，卖淫合法，嫖娼违法，就是这么梦幻
en: Indeed, in many Western countries today, selling sex is legal while buying it is unlawful — quite the fantasy.

text: 阶段三：你不买，我卖给谁啊，速速解禁“购买”（女权3.0）个别西方国家已经进化到这个时代
en: Stage three: if you don't buy, who do I sell to? Lift the ban on 'buying' at once (feminism 3.0) — a few Western countries have already evolved to this era.

text: 随着女性投身这个行当，她们发现，在男性“购买违法”的境况下，自己的收入受到了很大影响，自己从事的“合法行业”，居然因为消费者“违法”导致收入低下，仙女怎么能忍受自己“收入低”呢
en: As women entered this trade, they found that with men's 'buying unlawful', their own income took a big hit; their 'legal profession' earned little precisely because consumers were 'unlawful' — how could these fairies tolerate their own 'low income'?

text: 于是，各国的女权再次走上街头，要求废除购买违法，为自己的收入提升勇敢发声：
en: So the feminists of various countries took to the streets again, demanding the repeal of the ban on buying, boldly speaking up for their own income boost:

text: “处罚嫖客=杀死妓女”
en: 'Punishing clients = killing prostitutes'

text: 至于“卖春”行业兴盛必然带来的“人口买卖”问题，仙女哪在乎这个。
en: As for the 'human trafficking' inevitably brought by a thriving 'sex-selling' industry, these fairies couldn't care less.

text: 自己的利益当然优先于“girl help girl ”
en: Their own interests naturally take priority over 'girl help girl'.

text: 随着荷兰等国家对于卖淫的全面解禁，欧洲的人口贩卖问题直线上升，但是女权主义者获得了真正的自由，一切都是值得的（PS:中国是欧盟人口贩卖的第二大“货源地”）
en: As countries like the Netherlands fully decriminalised prostitution, human trafficking in Europe rose sharply — yet feminists gained true freedom, and it was all worth it (PS: China is the EU's second-largest 'source' for human trafficking).

text: 我国的“卖淫合法化”议题
en: Our country's 'prostitution legalisation' debate

text: 目前也是由女性，在“维护女性权益”的旗帜之下，实质推动的
en: is currently being substantively driven by women, under the banner of 'safeguarding women's rights and interests'.
